assessment: This is an important article that is methodologically compelling that provides evidence that an unhealthy lifestyle during adolescence accelerates epigenetic age in adulthood and that these associations are largely explained by the effect of shared genetic influences. The main strengths of this article are the relatively large sample size, longitudinal assessment of lifestyle factors, and sophisticated statistical analyses. The article will be of interest to a broad audience, including individuals working on methylation, epidemiology, and/or aging.
